decisions.statement: The call is read against the page handed in rather than flags spelled here.
The work is handed what the call said, under the keys the argument pages name.
A call the reader refuses is answered with those reasons and no work runs.
A work that threw after writing names in its refusal what that run had written.
A call is read, refused or run through one act here rather than by each command.
A command names the act to run and states nothing of how a call is read.
Nothing here leaves the work for a command to open itself.
A command catching what its own seam throws is written without this act.
Nothing here adds to the reasons the reader gave.
A command whose refusal is built from that list is written without this act.
Nothing here spells a flag, so which arguments a command takes is on its page.
Nothing here reads a file or writes one.

definition: the one way into a command, its call read against that command's own page
